title: Charbit's spectral short-cycle conjecture: the sharp digon case and a Perron-period obstruction
exact_target: Does a large adjacency spectral radius force a short directed cycle with the proposed threshold $n/k$?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $G$ be a finite simple directed graph on $n\geq1$ vertices, with no loops and at most one arc for each ordered pair of distinct vertices.
Opposite arcs are allowed; when both occur, they form a directed cycle of length two.
Its adjacency matrix $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ has $A_{ij}=1$ exactly when $i\to j$ is an arc and has zero diagonal.
The spectral radius is
\[
 \rho(A)=\max\{|\lambda|:\lambda\in\mathbb C,
                       \det(\lambda I-A)=0\}.
\]
Although $A$ need not be symmetric, the radius is a well-defined nonnegative real number.
A directed cycle of length $\ell$ consists of distinct vertices $v_1,\ldots,v_\ell$ with arcs $v_i\to v_{i+1}$ and $v_\ell\to v_1$.

Charbit's proposed spectral version of a short-cycle bound asks whether, for every integer $k\geq2$,
\[
 \rho(A)\geq\frac nk
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 G\text{ contains a directed cycle of length at most }k.
\]
Equivalently, every digraph avoiding directed cycles of lengths $2,\ldots,k$ should satisfy the strict inequality $\rho(A)<n/k$.
The boundary equality is included in the hypothesis and therefore cannot be discarded.
The condition uses the spectral radius of the original adjacency matrix, not its symmetric part, a singular value, or a degree average.
The graph is not assumed regular or strongly connected.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does a large adjacency spectral radius force a short directed cycle with the proposed threshold $n/k$?
